conflicts.topic: Current AFSA full-licence wording versus public derivatives surfaces
conflicts.resolution: Treat futures/options/copy-trading as publicly surfaced in Kazakhstan, but do not overstate the current AFSA full-register wording as expressly naming every derivatives sub-product.
conflicts.notes: The sandbox register explicitly named futures/options later than the 2022 grant, while the current full register uses broader regulated-activity language.

conflicts.topic: Technical reachability versus legal authorization versus resident eligibility
conflicts.resolution: Public reachability and sign-up affordances were recorded separately from local authorization and actual successful resident onboarding.
conflicts.notes: This implements the task's non-collapse rule.

conflicts.topic: Public referral offer visibility versus Kazakhstan eligibility and CBW campaign verification
conflicts.resolution: The offer is visible, some restricted-jurisdiction rules are public, Kazakhstan-specific eligibility remains unconfirmed, and CBW-specific binding is blocked until an owner-approved campaign input exists.
conflicts.notes: Verification is capped below account-confirmed level by task design.

conflicts.topic: Binance Card global product pages versus Kazakhstan-specific eligibility
conflicts.resolution: Kazakhstan-specific Mastercard cash withdrawal exists as a fiat rail, but the reviewed Binance Card program pages do not explicitly confirm Kazakhstan as an eligible Binance Card issuance market.
conflicts.notes: Do not infer Binance Card availability from a card cash-out rail.

conflicts.topic: Snippet-only announcement evidence versus direct-page evidence
conflicts.resolution: Kept these records as official but partial/snippet-only evidence and downgraded their verification state accordingly.
conflicts.notes: This addresses the Issue #84 correction request to downgrade snippet-only records.

conflicts.topic: Regulator FAQ monthly funding cap versus Binance rail guides without a visible fixed cap
conflicts.resolution: The regulator-side monthly retail funding cap was recorded as a legal/regulatory constraint, while Binance rail guides were recorded as operational how-to pages without forcing a fixed cap into each guide.
conflicts.notes: This avoids falsely treating guide-level fee/amount interfaces as exhaustive legal-limit disclosures.
